notes.title: Shadows Over Solis Pre-Release Event: March 8th
notes.notes:
Welcome to our final article for Forging Shadows over Solis! Today, we have an electrifying preview of something the story has been building toward since the very first storyline event. But before we dive in, don’t forget to sign up for the Shadows over Solis Prerelease event happening this Saturday! Secure your spot now: https://events.solforgefusion.com/event/H5KDA81A5W

Now that you’re all set, let’s get into it!

The Darkness Within

Since the launch of the game, players have heard whispers of the Blight—a darkness seeking to claim the heart of the Forgeborn and consume the world of Solis. Over the last year, we’ve discovered its true name: the Darkforge. As the world begins to thaw, a new era dawns, but so does an ancient and terrible threat! When designing how the Darkforge would take shape in the game, we explored many possibilities. Ultimately, given its corrupting influence within the Factions, we wanted it to introduce corrupted cards into a Faction deck while still allowing access to other cards from that Faction. But that raises a critical question: which Forgeborn will lead these Darkforge decks?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/3f4d64a38834b43aaea3aadc55687adce131df13.png

Among the Forgeborn, Sunder has fallen the farthest under the Darkforge’s sway. Now, she serves as a Blighted Forgeborn, fully devoted to its sinister will. But a force as powerful as the Darkforge requires more than one leader.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/f0be57de22b12e8b795d3f5d4738a43f518a69f7.png

The Darkforge has also claimed the soul of Cercee, who once sacrificed herself to halt its spread. Now, the undead queen rises again, commanding a new army to lay claim to Solis!

But the Darkforge’s corruption is not limited to Nekrium and Tempys. As its influence spreads, it seeks to consume Alloyin and Uterra as well! Blighted Cercee and Blighted Sunder can be found in all 4 factions!

When a deck has one of these Blighted Forgeborn the corruption also affects the deck allowing for some familiar faces to join.

I Give Into Temptation!

One of the most unforgettable moments from the very first Fuse Fest event was players shouting, “I give into temptation!” to gain power. We knew this had to be reflected in the game, and it became a core theme for the Darkforge. As you can see with Blighted Sunder and Blighted Cercee, these Forgeborn grant immense power—at the cost of your own Health. The more you sacrifice, the greater your rewards. This philosophy extends across all Darkforge cards. The Darkforge’s creatures are not new faces. These are familiar beings from the first three sets of SolForge Fusion, now twisted and reborn under the Darkforge’s influence!

Take the Metamind Overseer. Originally, it granted a single Gizmo or Mega Gizmo. But as the Metamind Omenseer, it offers even more summoning potential—at the price of your Health.

The Darkforge gave us the opportunity to design creatures with abilities stronger than what is typically seen at their Levels. This introduces an engaging new playstyle where your Health becomes a resource. Mastering this balance is the key to victory when piloting a Darkforge deck.

And if you manage your Health wisely, the Darkforge will reward your devotion handsomely!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/72cccc1f55a375f2d71ade80d61f5e416b8dcdfa.png

Those who prove their loyalty to the Darkforge gain access to a free damage spell—efficient removal that helps keep you in the game as you teeter on the edge. Meeting specific Health thresholds is a powerful incentive to embrace this archetype, but it’s not the only way to unlock your Darkforge cards’ true potential!

These corrupted versions of familiar creatures grow even stronger as long as you’ve taken damage during your turn, rewarding aggressive, risk-taking play with instant benefits.

Join us in discord to see more spoilers this week!

The Darkforge allowed us to dive deep into an omni-faction archetype that fully integrates the Forgeborn. We can’t wait to see what devastating power you’ll unleash when Shadows over Solis arrives! Keep an eye out for more previews from the SolForge Fusion community this week as we approach the Shadows over Solis Prerelease event. See you there!

Would you like to know more?
https://www.solforgefusion.com/post/forging-shadows-over-solis:-darkforge-rising

notes.title: Shadows Over Solis Pre-Release Event: March 8th
notes.notes:
Welcome back, fellow Forgeborn! Today we're taking a trip down memory lane and looking at the results of some of our previous storyline events and how those have shaped the design of Shadows over Solis. Players will be able to get their hands on the new set as soon as Saturday, March 8th at the pre-release event, and the set will release officially on Satuday, March 15th.

Shadows Over Solis: A World Shaped by Your Choices

The world of SolForge Fusion continues to evolve with its newest expansion, Shadows Over Solis. This set is not just a collection of new cards; it’s a milestone that reflects the collective impact of players’ decisions in both physical and digital storyline events. For newcomers and veterans alike, the release of Shadows Over Solis is a chance to see how player participation has influenced the narrative and mechanics of the game, while diving deeper into the ever-expanding lore of SolForge Fusion and the world of Solis.

The Birth of the Metaminds

The Alloyin’s journey in Shadows Over Solis began at Origins with the event Forging Destiny, where Crux Cobalt’s history and master plan were crafted by fans. Crux’s vision of a hivemind network became a reality through a series of player-driven outcomes, leading to the rise of Metamind creatures. This technological marvel isn’t just a thematic expansion; it’s a gameplay innovation. In Set 4, Alloyin players will gain access to a host of Metamind creatures, reinforcing their dominance as the faction of intellect and innovation.

Sacrifice and Shadows in Nekrium

Cercee’s tale took a dramatic turn during Fuse Fest 2024, where players uncovered a rebellion within the city of Shroud, spearheaded by the Forgeborn Nix Nekyia and their clandestine group known as “The Resurrection.” The rebellion’s discovery prompted Cercee to recruit more assassins into her elite guard, the Queen’s Knives, to eliminate the threat. This influx of warriors expanded Nekrium’s ranks, resulting in more warrior card-types for the Nekrium faction in this new set.

Amidst this turmoil, Toxys Mori, the leader of Cercee’s elite guard, was revealed as a traitor. Cercee’s attempt to assassinate Toxys forced her to flee, embarking on the pilgrimage to the SolForge. There, Toxys emerged as a powerful new Forgeborn, reshaping the balance of power within Nekrium.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/b9fc4d4ddc47d601114c1d684f10edc263523a51.png

[Some information about the Nekrium's story has been redacted!!]

Tempys Secures Whitefang Pass

For Tempys, the events of UKGE 2023 marked a monumental shift, redefining the faction both culturally and as an emerging world power. Tempys players’ choices won them Whitefang Pass, a vital trade corridor that reshaped the boundaries between factions. This victory not only granted Tempys a strategic advantage but also paved the way for their first non-nomadic settlement. Shadows Over Solis will see Whitefang Pass added to the Tempys faction as a new Exalt.

The Tempys faction’s story also welcomes a new Forgeborn, Tundra, who represents an element of the growing divisions among the Tempys clans. These divisions split into three paths: those who follow the power-hungry and corrupted Sunder, those who adhere to the ancient and dogmatic ways of Korok, and those who choose a third path, embodying a new path we will likely explore at future events. Her arrival in Shadows Over Solis is accompanied by a surge of yeti creature cards, bringing fresh possibilities to the Tempys playstyle. This story is deeply rooted in the deck lore surrounding Sylka, an ancient yeti who heroically sacrificed herself for her kin, inspiring Tundra's path to the SolForge.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/311a0e167c309f57b4d93337ffb95761b5eb370e.png

Redemption in Uterra

The Uterra faction’s arc has been one of redemption and renewal. At Gen Con 2024, players witnessed Oros’ cleansing from the corruption of the Blight and his reunion with Ironbeard. Once consumed by the DarkForge in a desperate attempt to save his people, Oros now stands as a symbol of healing. His redemption mirrors Uterra’s broader narrative shift towards unity and collaboration. This theme is further explored in the Scorchwyrm Online Event, where players helped tame the terrifying Scorchwyrm, forging a bond between Oros and Nova.

[Some information about the Uterra story has been redacted!!]
The unity of the Forgeborn in the Uterran cause is the foundation for a new mechanic in Shadows Over Solis. This mechanic encourages Uterra players to strategically position their creatures adjacent to one another, creating powerful synergies representing the faction’s lore-derived focus on collaboration.

Exploring Deck Lore

Deck Lore is custom-tailored lore about one of the SolForge decks. Players who participate in storyline events have the opportunity to immortalize their decks through custom-written short stories permanently attached to their registered decks.

For example, the Tempys faction’s journey in Shadows Over Solis draws heavily from the tale of Sylka, an ancient yeti whose heroic sacrifice continues to influence her kin—maritime sea shanties and a deck full of yetis inspired this lore.

To have deck lore written, participants generally need to attend a storytelling event and recount an exciting moment from a match. While this is the most common way, there are no hard and fast rules about how or when deck lore is created—the decision ultimately lies with the Stone Blade team. A handful of these submissions are selected, and the details provided are used to create stories attached to the decks, immortalizing them on solforgefusion.com. 

On our story page, you can find all the SolForge Lore, including deck lore.

A Story You Helped Forge

Every event, every decision, and every sacrifice made by players has left a mark on Shadows Over Solis. From Cercee’s rise to power to the taming of the Scorchwyrm, the set was crafted from a player-driven narrative. The choices made at SolForge Fusion events have influenced the storyline and shaped the cards and mechanics that define this set.

As Shadows Over Solis launches, it’s clear that the world of SolForge Fusion is as dynamic and collaborative as the players who bring it to life. Whether you’re a seasoned veteran or a curious newcomer, now is the perfect time to jump into the fray and see how your choices can shape the future of Solis.

In the end, the story is yours to forge.

Would You Like to Know More?
https://solforgefusion.com/post/shadows-over-solis:-bridging-story-and-mechanics

 Cercee’s Propaganda should now give the buff when the enemy creature is in the same lane as one of your exalts.
 Rooted Leafkin should not have his passive ability on your other creatures.

notes.title: New Shop Experience and Quest Changes
notes.notes:
Updated Shop 
We've made a number of revisions to our shop interface in a continuing effort to improve the experience for our users. Items have been grouped more appropriately for ease of purchase and players will now receive notifications when new shop items are available.

 Quests 
We have updated our quest system from your feedback. Players will now gain one quest every 4 hours and will have the ability to delete unwanted quests.

 Bug Fixes 

 Nuada, Faith’s Flourish L2 and L3 effect will now trigger when a creature enters into a lane with an exalt.
 Sunder's Outwit Forgeborn power now can no longer have an enemy creature strike itself.
 Overgrown allows the enemy player to play up to two cards instead of just one.
 Fraud’s Experiment creature’s Activate abilities now work correctly.
 Cercee's Graverobbery Forgebron power now triggers Savant creature effects.
 Cercee's Graverobbery Forgeborn power now puts the stolen creature back in the appropriate banish pile when destroyed.
 When a creature has had its keywords removed, they now can gain those keywords again in the same turn.
 Cypien Experimentation no longer plays a gizmo when played normally.
 Conscript the Dead no longer gives an enemy creature a debuff if none of your creatures are destroyed.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/62a3e9f9bd2575eacb76a8e32abd9ff1e2b2a4c2.png

notes.title: Card Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
We have a smaller but important update as we have a collection of individual card bug fixes!

Bug Fixes

 Slay keyword now should not trigger from destroying your own creatures.
 Elementalist Knights exalted ability triggers correctly.
 Duplication Dome level 3 should now target the creature with the deploy effect and not itself when gaining buffs.
 Spiteful creatures will now target the opposing creature when destroyed.
 Cypien Experimentation now plays a gizmo when upgraded.
 Hantu, the Restless now says which creature is being reanimated when the player is making the choice to take damage or have the creature reanimate.
 If both players have a card that transforms, playing their card will only transform their creature/exalt.
 Effects like Necrotic creatures that let you play up to one creature when it is destroyed will let you say no and not play the creature.
 Web should now blank passive abilities (card text is not blanked though when right clicked).
 Korok - Deep Burn should successfully stop enemy players from healing.
 Blighted Ironbeard - Shield Slam (unfortunately still the wrong name) now deals excess damage to the enemy player.
 Blighted Ironbeard - Alloyin Steel (unfortunately still the wrong name) should now deal damage to the opposing creature.


Known Bug

 For effects like Necrotic, if you say no, visually the creature card will stay in front of your hand until you undo an action. This is a visual bug and you still can play cards from your hand.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/62a3e9f9bd2575eacb76a8e32abd9ff1e2b2a4c2.png

notes.title: Quality of Life Fixes, Matchmaking changes
notes.notes:
Gameplay 

 Matchmaking will attempt to match you to players closer to your level. We have now implemented a matchmaking system to track your wins with specific decks and queues you closer to players with similar deck elo.
 Cannot undo after Crux Cobalt’s Mind Over Matter or Determined Choice (These reveal new information to the player).
 Reduced XP thresholds for first 2 decks on Player XP Track to 500xp and 5000xp.
 New user flow updates - New users can access the settings when they first open the game and after the tutorial when the user presses play they will be put into the campaign
 We have removed the first encounter's passive abilities in the campaign. These are all the forgeborn encounters. We want these first encounters to be an easy start to the campaign and at this moment the average win rate between these encounters is 71%. We are looking for this to be closer to 90%. So as a first change we are just removing these extra abilities and making them closer to a regular game of SolForge Fusion.
 New temp upgrades:
 Blazing Sol Stone: When you play a creature, if you have the Forge, it gets +A equal to the current cycle. Otherwise, it gets +H equal to the current cycle.
 Umbral Sol Stone: When you play a spell, if you have the Forge, deal 2 damage to the enemy player. Otherwise, you gain +2H.
 Blasted Battlefield: At the start of combat, if you have no empty lanes, your creatures get +3A.
 Digitization Module: At the start of combat, give one of your creatures +3A. If it is your only creature in play, give it +3H.
 Uttera Charger's Horn: At the start of combat, one of your creatures Battles an enemy creature.

UI

 Collection, Deck Select, and Fuse Decks load in pages rather than showing all decks at once. (Should make collection management for large collections less laggy)
 Added digital/physical deck filter toggles, updated filter tooltip for the former “Digital” to be the more accurate “Starter”.
 Blighted Forgeborns have card art. Names in-client changed from Exalted to Blighted
 Added deck filter to Fuse Decks menu
 Visual representation in end-game stats when you have reached max XP on a deck
 Fixes to triggers overlapping confirm/cancel and similar choices
 Tutorial game over screen shows tutorial deck
 Campaign map control improved: Can zoom in and out with scroll wheel, map moves around more smoothly, intro shows boss
 Some awkward UI around confirm/cancels improved for Storm Caller, Hantu, and Flame Jet

General Bugfixes

 Hivemind Pact Lv. 3 Doesn’t crash multiplayer game.
 Metamind Enhancer and Metamind Synapse ability works.
 Crux cobalt determined choice shows opponent’s hand.
 Steel rosetta augment doesn’t cause error out of multiplayer game.

Set 3 Bug Fixes

 Blighted forgeborn after transform should properly match the level + exhausted state.
 Blighted Ironbeard’s Sovereign Pillars no longer gains energy counters even if there is no creature in its lane
 Elementalist Knight exalt ability works

Known Issues

 Your matchmaking elo will not update until you log out and log back in
 Cercee Soul Swap Lv 3 crashes multiplayer games
 Cypien Experimentation doesn’t work correctly
 AI using Uterra charger Lv 3 will hang game
Friend battles might take a bit to match if your elos are far apart


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44821897/a1842725b67518bef00713c0197044bc44e80bd7.png

notes.title: New Patch and Updates
notes.notes:
Things We Added/Changed

Reclusa ascension powers have changed. At levels 1,6,10 you now will receive a base -5 in health instead of losing health every turn. Please let us know what you think.
We have new temp upgrades added to the available upgrades during the campaign! They are:
Glowhive Carapace - When one of your Beast creatures is destroyed, you get +3H.
Steggadon Boneyard - When one of your Dinosaurs is destroyed, your other creatures get +2A.
Emberlight Shard - When one of your Mage creatures is destroyed, deal 3 damage to the enemy player.
Oreian Flashbang - When one of your Robots is destroyed, enemy creatures get -2A.
Salvage-a-tron - When one of your Scientists is destroyed, play up to one Gizmo Minion.
Well of Lost Spirits - When one of your Spirit creatures is destroyed, deal 2 damage to the enemy player. Then, you get +2H.
Arragal Arena - When one of your Warriors is destroyed, deal 3 damage to an enemy creature.
Deck level cap increased to 21 (will allow you to earn the last foiled card)
XP rewards display updated
Set 2 decks on Player XP track are snowy
Timer changes color as it ticks down
Display whether opponent forfeited at end of PVP game

Things We Fixed

Viewing deck gallery while leveling up from main menu no longer causes UI raycast issues
Epoch Soldier plays correctly in Multiplayer
Blighted forgeborns add special graphics to game board
Blighted forgeborn art added
Rooted leafkin works
Steel Rosetta’s Boost works
Alloyin Monolith gives armor to creature and the destroys itself
Ghox’s Central Conductor transforms with a counter on it

Known Bugs

We are looking into issues with temp upgrades that affect creature types not stacking with the temp upgrades that make all your creatures that creature type.
We are working on effects triggering off of upgrading not working
We are aware of the spiteful adjective not giving the opposing creature the debuff upon death.

notes.title: Magic creator's new tabletop CCG now has an official Steam version
notes.notes:
Last time we checked in on SolForge Fusion - the latest game from Magic: the Gathering and Artifact designer Richard Garfield - it was gearing up for its launch on tabletops as a physical card game that would at some point also be playable in Tabletop Simulator. Now it's getting its own official digital version, and you can try the demo out now on Steam.
